How to Ship a Customer Order

Epicor > Customer Shipment Entry — step by step, with screenshots.

Steps

  1. Create a new pack
  2. Load the order (Mass Shipment)
  3. Set the quantities
  4. Create the UPS shipment
  5. Enter tracking number and weight
  6. Add the FREIGHT OUT charge
  7. Check the Summary tab
  8. Save and mark Shipped
  9. Print, save PDF, and email
  10. Remove a part from inspection
  11. Fix quantities adjusted too early
  12. If something goes wrong

Quick flow

The short version, in order. Each step is explained below.

  1. Order #
  2. Mass Shipment
  3. Ship All
  4. Check Inv Ship Qty
  5. Update and Save
  6. Tracking #
  7. Header
  8. New charge: FREIGHT OUT
  9. Save
  10. Summary
  11. Shipped

1Create a new pack

  • Open Customer Shipment Entry.
  • Click the New icon at the top left (the first icon in the toolbar) and choose New Pack.
  • You get a blank Pack: 0. The Pack ID is assigned when you save.

2Load the order (Mass Shipment)

  • Click Order Number... and pick the sales order, or type the order number into the field.
  • Check the Ship To and Ship Via shown on the pack match the order before you go on.
  • Click Mass Shipment. The order lines appear in Shipment Lines, and Epicor gives the pack an ID.
After loading, the Order Number field shows 0 again. That is normal. The lines are already on the pack.
If the grid stays empty, nothing on the order is ready to ship. Check that the release is firm, the part has stock in a warehouse and bin, and the order is not on hold.

3Set the quantities

  • Click Ship All to ship every line in full, or type the quantity under Inv Ship Qty on each line.
  • Check Inv Ship Qty on every line. It must match what is actually in the box. A line left at 0.00 does not ship.
  • If you are sending only part of a line, type the real quantity you are sending in Inv Ship Qty. The rest stays open on the order for the next shipment.
  • If a line is not going in this box at all, set its Inv Ship Qty to 0 or delete that line from the pack.
  • Click Update so the totals refresh with the new quantities.
  • Click the Save icon.
Negative on-hand popup. When you ship, Epicor may say "This transaction will result in a negative onhand quantity for Part ... Bin ... Do you want to continue?"
  • Clicking Yes ships it anyway and leaves the bin at a negative quantity.
  • Better: click No, fix the stock first (receive, pass inspection, or move it to the bin shown), then ship again.
  • Only click Yes if your supervisor says the stock count will be corrected afterward.

4Create the UPS shipment

  • Open UPS CampusShip in your browser and choose Create a Shipment.
  • Copy the Ship To name and address from the Epicor screen.
  • Enter the package weight and choose the service that matches Ship Via in Epicor (for example STANDARD GROUND or NEXT DAY).
  • Finish the shipment. UPS shows the Tracking Number and the Total Charges. Write both down.

5Enter the tracking number and weight

  • Back in Epicor, on the Summary tab, paste the UPS number into Tracking Number (it starts with 1Z).
  • Enter the Weight and keep the unit as LB.
  • Click the Save icon so the tracking number is kept.

6Add the FREIGHT OUT charge

  1. Go to the Header tab, then the Misc Charges sub-tab.
  2. Click the New icon (hover shows "New...").
  3. In Charge ID, open the dropdown and choose FREIGHT OUT. The other choice, Shipping Material, is for packaging.
  4. Type the dollar amount in Charge Amount. Use the Total Charges from UPS (for example 10.69).
  5. Click the Save icon. FREIGHT OUT now shows under Misc Charges in the tree on the left.
Add the charge only once. If FREIGHT OUT is already in the tree, open it and fix the amount instead of adding a second one.

7Check the Summary tab

  • Open the Summary tab.
  • Check the Tracking Number and Weight are filled in.
  • Check the freight amount shows in the totals and matches the UPS Total Charges.
  • Check the number of lines and quantities match the box one last time.

8Save and mark Shipped

  • Click the Save icon.
  • Go to the Summary tab and tick Shipped.
  • Save again. The Status changes from OPEN to SHIPPED.
Once the status is SHIPPED the pack is locked. Check the quantities, tracking number and freight charge before you tick the box.

9Print, save PDF, and email

  1. In UPS CampusShip, under Print Shipping Documents, tick Label. Tick Receipt only if you need it.
  2. Set "Print labels using my UPS thermal printer?" to Yes for the label printer, or No to print to a normal printer or PDF.
  3. Click Print. To keep a copy, choose Save as PDF as the printer and click Save.
  4. In Epicor, print the packing slip from Actions or the print icon.
  5. Weigh and pack the box, put the label on, and email the PDF to Amanda.

Remove a part from inspection

A part that is still in inspection is not in stock, so it cannot ship. Pass it out of inspection first.

  1. Open Inspection Processing.
  2. Enter your Inspector ID.
  3. Find the part in the inspection list. Search by Part, PO or Job if the list is long.
  4. Select the line and open it for inspection.
  5. Enter the Passed Quantity. Enter a Failed Quantity only for parts that are rejected.
  6. Set the Warehouse and Bin the part goes to. Use the same bin the shipment ships from.
  7. Click the Save icon. The part leaves inspection and is now on hand in that bin.
  8. Go back to Customer Shipment Entry and ship it.
Failed parts do not go to stock. They go to a DMR for review. Tell your supervisor when you fail a part.

Fix quantities adjusted too early

If someone adjusted the stock before the part was received, passed inspection or shipped, the bin is now off. Undo the early adjustment, then do the steps in the right order.

  1. Open Part Transaction History Tracker and enter the part number.
  2. Find the early adjustment (transaction type ADJ-QTY). Note the quantity, Warehouse, Bin and date.
  3. Open Quantity Adjustment and enter the same Part, Warehouse and Bin.
  4. Enter the opposite amount in Adjust Quantity. If +5 was added too early, enter -5.
  5. Pick a Reason Code and add a note such as "Reverse early adjustment".
  6. Click the Save icon and check the on-hand quantity in the bin is back to what it was.
  7. Now do the normal steps in order: receive, pass inspection, then ship.
Check with your supervisor before you adjust stock. Never adjust a shipped pack. If the wrong quantity was already shipped, see the table below.

If something goes wrong

ProblemFix
Grid is empty after Mass ShipmentThe order has nothing ready. Check stock, release status, holds, and the site.
Line ships at 0 qtyInv Ship Qty is 0.00. Type the quantity or click Ship All, then Update.
Negative on-hand popupClick No and fix the stock or bin. See step 3.
Part is stuck in inspectionPass it to stock in Inspection Processing first, then ship. See Remove a part from inspection.
Stock was adjusted too earlyReverse the early adjustment, then redo the steps in order. See Fix quantities adjusted too early.
Freight charge shows twiceDelete the extra FREIGHT OUT line under Header → Misc Charges before you mark Shipped, then save.
Shipped by mistake or wrong quantityAsk your supervisor. It must be reversed with an offsetting transaction. Do not delete it.
No FREIGHT OUT in the dropdownCheck you are on Header → Misc Charges, and that the charge exists for your site.
